newsitem.title: USA: U.S. retailers blame cold spring for mixed sales.
newsitem.headline: U.S. retailers blame cold spring for mixed sales.

text.p: Retailers Thursday reported mixed sales for May, blaming cold spring weather that left fans, grills, summer clothes and other seasonal products collecting dust on store shelves.
Retail sales have eroded steadily since the start of the year, hurt by cool weather, weaker employment gains and slower economic growth, analysts said.

Most retailers reported modest sales gains for May but a few, including Sears, Roebuck and Co. and Gap Inc., posted flat results or sales declines. Analysts said discounting of unsold goods probably would hurt second-quarter profits.
"There's too much inventory in the retail industry," said Patrick McCormack of Alex. Brown & Sons Inc. "Earnings estimates are vulnerable to downward revisions."

A Salomon Brothers index of same-store sales, or sales of stores open a year, rose 2.4 percent in May, compared with a 5.2 percent gain in May 1996. The index has declined steadily since January when it rose by 7.3 percent, Salomon said.
"Much of the strength early in the year was borrowed from strength later in the year," said Diane Swonk, deputy chief economist at First Chicago NBD Corp.
Wal-Mart Stores Inc., the nation's largest retailer, said sales at stores open a year rose 3.6 percent in May compared to a 5 percent rise a year earlier.
Kmart Corp. said same-store sales rose 2.7 percent, and Sears, Roebuck and Co. posted a decline of 1.2 percent.

"Kmart's sales for the month were below plan due primarily to cold weather," said Kmart Chairman Floyd Hall. "This affected sales of seasonal goods such as selected apparel, horticulture, and camping."
While consumer confidence remains high, shoppers have cut spending because of slower employment gains, a tightening of credit and slower economic growth generally.
"We have some fundamental slackening in the consumer sector," said Swonk of First Chicago.
The weather dampened business especially in the Midwest and Northeast last month, retailers said.
"In regions not affected by cool weather, such as the Northwest and Southwest, overall sales were strong," Sears Chief Executive Arthur Martinez said in a statement.

Other retailers with operations in regions where weather was gloomy reported declines. Bensalem, Pa.-based Charming Shoppes Inc. said same-store sales fell 4 percent and Waban Inc., of Natick, Mass., said sales at its BJ's Wholesale Club fell 1.5 percent in May.
"Consumer confidence is strong, but the weather kept the reins on sales of seasonal merchandise across all categories east of the Mississippi," said Todd Slater of Lazard Freres & Co.
Speciality clothing chains had poor results. Gap Inc. said sales were flat in May. Limited Inc.'s sales fell 7 percent.
Department stores reported mixed results.
Saks Holdings Inc. said sales rose 5 percent and May Department Stores Co., parent of Lord & Taylor and Robinsons-May, posted a 4 percent gain in May.
But Federated Department Stores Inc., parent of Rich's, Stern's, Macy's and Bloomingdale's, said sales rose just 2.5 percent.
Dayton Hudson Corp. said sales at its Marshall Field's, Dayton's and Hudson's department stores fell 0.9 percent. But Target, its discount store division, saw sales rise 5.5 percent.
